messages:
maya: quick follow-up on the bundle-slimming shim idea i posted yesterday. short summary + rollout ask.

jon: tldr?

maya: we detect identical k/v pairs across spans in a single bundle and lift them into a small coalesced map inside our internal envelope. per-span attrs remain for overrides. goal: cut bytes/index writes for chatty services.

sam: sounds useful. a couple concerns: billing parity, sampling interaction, and query compatibility.

maya: agreed. parity measures: we synthesize billing_key into per-span attrs when needed so downstream sees same value. sampling: compaction runs before sampling so sampled outputs are unchanged. query compat: indexer will expand coalesced map at write-time.

liz: can we have a dry-run mode that emits telemetry about what would be compacted? helps tune rules without changing envelopes.

maya: yes, plan includes dry-run + telemetry stream (counts, bytes saved if applied, keys touched).

jon: rules: whitelist low-card keys (svc, env, region), blacklist PII/high-card (user_id, email, req_id), adaptive mode for others based on span-count and recent global-cardinality. defaults in RFC doc.

sam: validation plan?

maya: dual-ingest canary: keep raw and slim envelopes for 72h; compute billing_parity_rate, query_delta_count, bytes_saved_pct. rollback if billing_parity_rate > 0.1% or query deltas too many.

ingest-bot: canary pipeline created: ingest-bundle-slim-canary.

jon: i'll prototype shim with flags: --mode=dry-run|rewrite|noop and --rules-file. will add unit tests and a small perf bench.

liz: i'll POC indexer expansion and measure CPU delta. add feature-flag per-service for canary.

sam: i'll wire parity harness and sampling tests.

maya: owners noted. perf target: median added latency < 2ms; fail open if >5ms. aim for >=5% stored-byte reduction for targeted services. sync next Tue to review canary metrics. :thumbsup:

jon: ack, starting branch.
